subject: stan model compile fail on CentOS

messages.author: 275b133a3506805a
messages.subject: stan model compile fail on CentOS
parts:
Hi all,

One of our compute servers here is CentOS, and I compiled stan fine
(from git master) but then my model fails to compile, even though it
compiles fine on my Ubuntu laptop. Here's the output from make:
<http://paste.debian.net/17228/>

GCC and make are the appropriate versions:

$ lsb_release -a
LSB Version:
:base-4.0-amd64:base-4.0-noarch:core-4.0-amd64:core-4.0-noarch:graphics-4.0-amd64:graphics-4.0-noarch:printing-4.0-amd64:printing-4.0-noarch
Distributor ID: CentOS
Description: CentOS release 6.4 (Final)
Release: 6.4

$ g++ --version
g++ (GCC) 4.4.7 20120313 (Red Hat 4.4.7-3)

$ make --version
GNU Make 3.81
This program built for x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu

Any clues welcome!

Best
Dan
--
http://www.mcld.co.uk

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan model compile fail on CentOS
parts:
No idea what's going on, but maybe one of our Linux users
might be able to help.

A couple of questions that should help debugging:

1. Was this with the latest release of Stan (1.3.0), or
something newer from GitHub?

2. Could you send your model, as well?

This code's all going to change dramatically in our next
release (2.0.0, hopefully in a few weeks).

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan model compile fail on CentOS
parts:
The issue might be lies in the status of our repo.  Take a look of, for example, file
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/commits/master/src/stan/gm/command.hpp
It seems to have the commit after Stan 1.3 (that is, after 12 Apr 2013).

So you just want to use Stan 1.3, I think it is safer to use the packaged one that 
can be found from mc-stan.org. 

--
Jiqiang
